strengths: Novel principle-driven reduction theorem (Theorem 3.3) elegantly derives port-Hamiltonian structure from four physical axioms, avoiding rigid global templates
Exceptional physical fidelity: near-zero energy drift (10^-4 to 10^-5), momentum conservation at 10^-7 scale, and correct dispersion emerge structurally without explicit constraints

Comprehensive experimental validation spanning analytic benchmarks, physics-consistency diagnostics (5 metrics), OOD generalization (frequency/resolution/parameter shifts), real acoustic data, and extensive ablations
Superior data efficiency and robustness: maintains physics fidelity with fewer training samples and remains stable under OOD shifts where baselines diverge (Table 5)
Exceptional reproducibility with code to be released, detailed hyperparameters, multiple random seeds, and clear data generation procedures throughout appendices
Practical efficiency: O(N) sparse operations, substantially fewer parameters than baselines (642 vs 100k+), faster inference/training, lower memory (Table 15)
Clear presentation with excellent motivation, well-structured proofs, informative figures (especially Figure 1), and honest treatment of limitations
weaknesses: Limited scope of applicability: framework excels on linear/weakly nonlinear wave-like systems; unclear generalization to turbulence, phase transitions, strongly nonlinear materials, or systems with memory effects

Jacobian-level rather than global guarantees: Theorem 3.3 proves local (pointwise) reduction, not that full trajectories follow port-Hamiltonian form; Strang splitting integrator and CFL-guarding are not uniquely determined by theory

Limited real-world validation: The Well acoustic scattering is primary real dataset (single system); most validation on synthetic data with known structure; lacks validation across diverse physical domains

Restricted practical assumptions: quadratic, state-independent energy metric limits nonlinear constitutive laws; general nonconvex energies discussed but not explored; state-dependent coupling remains limited (Section 5.7)

Insufficient guidance on applicability: lacks systematic characterization of when method succeeds vs. fails; no validation that real physical systems actually satisfy the four axioms (e.g., empirical orientation covariance)
Scalability questions: all experiments 2D or small-scale; no 3D demonstrations; impact on large-scale problems unclear

Incomplete experimental scope: nonlinear benchmarks limited to polynomial lattice systems without Navier-Stokes or complex materials; no hyperparameter sensitivity analysis; mesh quality effects unexplored
